title: Current NAO adjustment left winter sea-level error above summer error at 60 European gauges in 2005-2024
abstract: We tested whether a current-month North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO) adjustment removes the larger winter error in monthly sea-level reconstruction. We used PSMSL and NOAA snapshots at 60 European gauges. Separate station fits used earlier years only. The test covers 2005-2024 and 1199 paired station-years. The baseline has calendar-month terms and a linear trend. The adjustment adds four seasonal NAO slopes. Winter mean squared error fell by 31.2%. The winter-to-summer error ratio fell from 5.97 to 4.25. Its adjusted conditional 95% three-year block interval was 2.75 to 6.48. The adjustment removed 36.8% of the winter-minus-summer error excess, with an interval of 8.7% to 57.6%. Cell weights, monthly NAO slopes and 20-year fits gave similar residual ratios. The result shows a limit of this linear adjustment on this network. It does not identify the cause of the remaining error. Monthly means do not measure flood extremes. The short test, revised data and uneven station coverage limit inference. The package gives code, source hashes, aggregate scores, numerical checks and a figure. Source records and monthly error tables remain external.

display.caption: NAO adjustment leaves larger winter errors. Left: later-year test root mean squared error. Right: adjusted winter-to-summer mean squared error ratio with paired 95% three-year block intervals. Models use earlier years for fitting. The concurrent NAO input makes this a reconstruction test.

citations.reason: Prior network and forecast benchmark informed station selection. This test measures remaining winter error after concurrent adjustment. Observations overlap.
